import sys

def longest_proper_prefix_suffix(s):
    n = len(s)
    if n == 0:
        return 0
    
    # Build the failure function (LPS array)
    lps = [0] * n
    length = 0  # length of the previous longest prefix suffix
    i = 1
    
    while i < n:
        if s[i] == s[length]:
            length += 1
            lps[i] = length
            i += 1
        else:
            if length != 0:
                length = lps[length - 1]
            else:
                lps[i] = 0
                i += 1
    
    # The longest proper prefix which is also a suffix
    # Must be proper, so it cannot equal the whole string
    result = lps[n - 1]
    
    # Since lps[i] is always < i by construction, result < n always
    # So result is always a proper prefix/suffix
    return result

def main():
    s = sys.stdin.readline().strip()
    result = longest_proper_prefix_suffix(s)
    print(result)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
